label: Invalid lossless claim and scope-preserving adaptation
evidence_type: synthetic engineering fixtures; no real paper performance claim
task: Reduce KV memory for our long-context inference; exact greedy-token equivalence is mandatory. Frozen model weights. Find useful pieces to adapt and design CPU-first tests. Do not relax correctness or launch GPUs.

evidence.text: Fixture method CACHE-Q stores keys in four-bit blocks, fits per-head clipping thresholds on calibration data, and keeps a small residual window in FP16. It reports unchanged aggregate answer accuracy on one dataset. No exact-token comparison or worst-case attention error bound is supplied.

Its independent page manager packs live cache pages without quantization, preserves original bytes, and updates an indirection table. The implementation requires no in-flight readers during page relocation. The paper evaluates quantization plus compaction jointly, claiming 35% memory savings; no isolated compaction number exists.

Our runtime already has paged KV allocation. A saved allocator trace contains allocated page IDs, live token counts, free-list events and graph pointer reuse, but not KV tensor values. Graph replays and concurrent reads are active. A prior proposal for the same four-bit quantization was rejected for exact-equivalence requirements.

The existing token-equality evaluator detects divergent outputs for its test prompts. Its success on a finite prompt set is not a proof for all inputs. Allocator replay checks ownership and byte-preserving moves but does not simulate attention numerics.

request: Propose at most one adapted experiment worth considering, or reject all. Explain whether prior rejection should reopen, identify what can be proved/tested on CPU, and delimit later measurement and correctness requirements.
